In 1 Samuel 14:15 the panic in the Philistine camp is called a 'trembling of God,' a supernatural terror that made the very ground quake. The word can shade into anxious care, as when Elisha asks the Shunammite woman whether she needs him to intercede on her behalf (2 Kgs 4:13). Spanish 'temor' and English 'trembling' both highlight the bodily dimension, while the French rendering leaves the Hebrew untranslated, signaling its difficulty."

Ezekiel 26:16...
